text.p: UTI Energy Corp said Monday it has completed the acquisition of the contract drilling operations of Southland Drilling Co Ltd.

UTI also completed a $50 million financing, comprised of $25 million in senior term debt furnished by Mellon Bank and $25 million in four-year senior subordinated notes purchased by funds managed by Canyon Capital Management LP, UTI said.

In addition to financing the contract drilling acquisition, UTI said it used the proceeds from the financing to strengthen its liquidity by retiring $18.7 million in short-term and intermediate-term debt.

UTI said it purchased the drilling operations of privately-owned Southland for about $27 million and 100,000 five-year warrants at an exercise price of $48 per UTI common share. The acquisition price reflected a price reduction of $750,000 based on UTI's election to pay in cash in lieu of issuing a $13 million promissory note for a portion of the acquisition.

UTI said the retired debt included an $8 million two-year promissory note issued in the Viersen & Cochran acquisition completed in August 1996. The prepayment of the Viersen note allowed UTI to take advantage of a $345,000 discount for early payment.

Additionally, UTI said, its revolving line of credit with Mellon Bank was paid down about $4 million leaving a $1.2 million balance, while increasing the borrowing limit of the revolving line of credit available to $12 million from $8.4 million. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
